claims.text: Electroless Cu pre-coating of W powders or skeletons before spark plasma sintering will produce a more defect-free W–Cu composite.
The resulting composite will be mechanically durable for fusion-reactor heat-transfer applications.
The electroless plating step will form a continuous, conformal Cu coating on W surfaces.
The conformal Cu coating will ensure intimate W–Cu interfacial contact during sintering.
Electroless Cu plating promotes uniform wetting between W and Cu during sintering.
Electroless Cu plating promotes diffusion bonding between W and Cu during sintering.
Improved wetting and diffusion bonding reduce phase separation in SPS-processed W–Cu.
Improved wetting and diffusion bonding reduce void formation in SPS-processed W–Cu.
Reduced phase separation and void formation improve the composite's thermal conductivity.
Reduced phase separation and void formation improve mechanical robustness under irradiation.
Electroless-plated SPS samples will have a lower void fraction than vapor-coated W powders processed by standard sintering.
Electroless-plated SPS samples will have superior thermal transport relative to the vapor-coated standard-sintering baseline.
Electroless-plated SPS samples will have superior mechanical durability relative to the vapor-coated standard-sintering baseline.
The predicted advantages will persist under cyclic thermal and irradiation stresses representative of fusion-reactor joints.
Vapor-coated W powders processed by standard sintering achieve near-perfect W–Cu contact.
The vapor-coated standard-sintering baseline still suffers from phase separation and residual void formation.
The proposed benefit is expected to be confined to SPS-fabricated composites used for heat transfer in fusion reactors.
The optimal Cu coating thickness and uniformity are not yet established.
The long-term stability of the electroless Cu coating under high irradiation is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The initial state and baseline are described as vapor-coated W, while the intervention is also a Cu pre-coating step; calling the vapor-coated control 'without pre-coating' is ambiguous unless it specifically means without electroless pre-coating.

The baseline is said to achieve 'near-perfect contact' while also being characterized as suffering from phase separation and residual void formation. These statements are not strictly mutually exclusive, but the extent and location of the remaining defects are not reconciled.
